comparator.name: Wiskunde (Mathematics)
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026-2027 programme appendix defines the ordinary Bachelor Wiskunde as 180 EC: a 135-EC Mathematics major and 45 EC of profiling space. The major contains 82.5 EC compulsory study, one 7.5-EC modelling choice, 15 EC of restricted choice and 30 EC of further Mathematics choice. The compulsory sequence includes proof, two integrated calculus-and-linear-algebra courses, analysis, groups and rings, programming, probability, multivariable analysis, topology and a 15-EC bachelor thesis. The generic normalized target does not name the separate Wiskunde & Toepassingen direction, so the ordinary Bachelor Wiskunde in Overview 1 is reconstructed and no route is selected. Where the ordinary programme requires choices, the first eligible courses in the formally adopted table order are used neutrally and independently of UCR provision: Modelling with ODEs and PDEs for the modelling choice; Discrete Mathematics and Complex Analysis for the 15-EC restricted choice; and Mathematics Lab, Multivariable Analysis, Mathematical Game Theory and Differentiable Manifolds for the 30-EC Mathematics choice. The 45-EC profiling space remains genuinely open. The public curriculum page corroborates the three-year structure, eight-course first year, mathematical subject progression, 45 EC of wholly free choice and the distinction between ordinary Mathematics study paths and the separate Mathematics & Applications direction.

exception.reason: Utrecht's ordinary Mathematics bachelor requires a cumulative proof-based core in calculus and linear algebra, analysis, abstract algebra, probability, multivariable analysis and topology, followed by restricted higher mathematics, a 15-EC mathematical thesis and additional advanced mathematical choice. UCR has a useful applied quantitative set but no proof-based sequence in analysis or abstract algebra, no topology or differential-geometry pathway, and no independent mathematics thesis. Even after using every directly relevant UCR mathematics course, most of the 23 non-PPD places in a UCR programme would have to be filled with computing, data science and applications that cannot substitute for this disciplinary progression. A 24-course alternative would therefore misrepresent the target rather than provide a defensible Mathematics programme.
exception.curriculumContext: The current formal programme accounts for all 180 EC as an 82.5-EC compulsory mathematical sequence, 7.5 EC of modelling, 15 EC of restricted Mathematics choice, 30 EC of further Mathematics choice and 45 EC of open profiling space. The required and selected major components still amount to 135 EC, including the 15-EC bachelor thesis. Choices were instantiated by official table order before UCR provision was assessed; the separate Mathematics & Applications direction was not substituted for the generic target.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods supplies applied calculus and linear-algebra tools; DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide valuable applied mathematical progression. DISARIN212 Logic & Discrete Mathematics adds formal and discrete reasoning, and DISARIN311 Optimization Methods in AI is a relevant application. The workbook does not contain a sustained proof-based real-analysis sequence, abstract algebra beyond introductory discrete material, topology, complex analysis, differentiable manifolds or a mathematics bachelor-thesis course. Programming, data-science, econometrics and AI courses support mathematical applications but cannot supply the missing disciplinary core or turn the remaining non-PPD course slots into a coherent Mathematics degree.
